description:
FILED s532a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-01), found probing #4164.  PRE-EXISTING (base 10cdc985 identical).  SILENT (output lost).

    open(O, ">-") or die "o: $!"; print O "11 stdout\n"; close O; print "after\n";
  perl 5.40.3: 11 stdout / after
  PCL: 11 stdout   ("after" never appears)

perl's 2-arg ">-" opens a handle on STDOUT's PerlIO; closing it does not close descriptor 1 for the program's STDOUT.  PCL's handle IS *standard-output* (or the fd stream) and close closes it.  Probe the "-" (STDIN) twin and `open(my $o, ">&STDOUT")` (a real dup, control).  Layer: cl/pcl-runtime.lisp p-close / the "-" arm of %p-open-impl.  Probe: scratch/s532a/p/op4.pl.

=== DONE (s536h) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08, commit 79b44e62, cl/ only).  The TWO-argument magic name `-` ("-", "<-", "+<-" -> STDIN; ">-", ">>-", "+>-", "+>>-" -> STDOUT) is now perl's IoTYPE_STD handle: a NEW handle on the standard stream's own buffer, `(%p-fdopen-alias STREAM t)` -- the fdopen alias marked :std -- so `close` detaches it only: true, no flush, $! untouched (doio.c io_close's IoTYPE_STD arm), and STDOUT stays open.  A second close is "" + EBADF (perl).  The THREE-argument form never means a standard stream: `open($f, ">", "-")` / `open($f, "<", "-")` open a FILE named "-" (probed 5.40.3) -- PCL wrote to STDOUT there, a silent wrong found in the same arm and fixed with it.  fileno of the alias is 1 / 0 (perl).  Guard Pl/t/open-modes-01.t row 9 (perl oracle; FAILS on the ba7863a3 extraction).  Left: ">-:raw" (#4721).
subject: close on a handle opened ">-" (or "-") closes the program's STDOUT: later prints are lost -- perl's close of that handle leaves STDOUT writable
